intent: Determine weekly purchase orders for the upcoming weekend promotion based on stock, expected sales, and vendor constraints.

definitions.name: Expected Sales
definitions.text: Start from each product's average over the last four weekends. Products on offer sell about 40% more, the kit's ingredients about 10% more, and everything else about 15% more. We expect to sell about 40 kits, and each one uses a loaf, a pack of avocados and a pack of feta on top of their own sales. Round up to whole units.

constants.quote: Products on offer sell about 40% more
We expect to sell about 40 kits

groups.quote: eggs, cherry tomatoes and rocket are on offer
a sourdough loaf, a pack of ripe avocados and a pack of feta

definitions.formula: ceil((double(record.weekend_1 + record.weekend_2 + record.weekend_3 + record.weekend_4) / double(constants.num_weekends)) * (key in groups.offer_products ? (1.0 + double(constants.offer_markup_pct) / 100.0) : (key in groups.kit_ingredients ? (1.0 + double(constants.kit_ingredient_markup_pct) / 100.0) : (1.0 + double(constants.other_markup_pct) / 100.0))) + (key in groups.kit_ingredients ? double(constants.expected_kits) : 0.0))

examples.why: Average sales for SD-01 is (28+31+30+31)/4 = 30; SD-01 is a kit ingredient, so it sells 10% more: 30 * 1.1 = 33; plus 40 kits: 33 + 40 = 73.
Average sales for EG-06 is (19+21+20+20)/4 = 20; EG-06 is on offer, so it sells 40% more: 20 * 1.4 = 28.
Average sales for LM-04 is (9+11+10+10)/4 = 10; LM-04 is everything else, so it sells 15% more: 10 * 1.15 = 11.5, rounded up to 12.

accounting.sentence: What this is for
Each week, suggest how many of each product to order for the coming Brunch weekend, so we have enough for what we expect to sell without overstocking.
A person checks and approves every order before it is placed.
The promotion
Brunch weekend runs every Saturday from 07:00 to Sunday 22:00.
The idea is to make avocado toast at home easy.
We sell an avocado toast kit (a sourdough loaf, a pack of ripe avocados and a pack of feta), and eggs, cherry tomatoes and rocket are on offer.
Ripe avocados don't keep.
How much we expect to sell
Start from each product's average over the last four weekends.
Products on offer sell about 40% more, the kit's ingredients about 10% more, and everything else about 15% more.
We expect to sell about 40 kits, and each one uses a loaf, a pack of avocados and a pack of feta on top of their own sales.
Round up to whole units.
What we have
Stock available is what we have on hand, less what is reserved, plus what arrives before the start.
Rules
Order in whole cases.
Never order more than the supplier can deliver.
Only order what arrives before Saturday's opening.
Only order what can still be placed before the supplier's cutoff for this weekend.
Aim for enough stock available to cover expected sales plus the category's safety margin. If that isn't possible, flag it for a person to decide.
If a product's stock count is older than its category allows, flag it for a person to decide, even when nothing is ordered.
Stock available plus the order must not exceed the ripe avocados we expect to sell.
